conviction_note: Nothing decisive found: the bar sits at or below the company's own Q3 guide midpoint, the insurance guide looks conservative against the Q2 exit run-rate, and the short has grown 35% since mid-August, all small positives; a new CFO's first call, the $1.0bn 2027 convert, a $283m all-BetterHelp goodwill balance and flat-to-weaker BetterHelp web traffic are small negatives. Findings sum to +0.8, and abs_move 11 at p_up 52 gives +0.44. The two agree in sign. p_up stays near 50 because the stock rose about 16% from $5.73 on 2026-10-20 to $6.655 into the print, on low volume, while the 25-delta skew pays 11.3 vol points for downside, and this name's reaction is set by the implied Q4/2027 BetterHelp cash-pay trajectory, which I could not observe.

findings.finding: The Q3 BetterHelp insurance guide of $25-31m (midpoint $28m) implies almost no sequential growth. Management said the last week of Q2 ran over 20,000 insurance sessions a week, an annualised run-rate above $110m, or about $27.5m a quarter, and insurance users rose more than 70% sequentially. The credentialed provider count went from about 4,500 to over 8,000 in two quarters (6,000+ at the Q1 call). If the run-rate merely held, Q3 lands at the midpoint; any session growth puts it at or above the $31m top. This is about $3-5m of upside on a $589m revenue midpoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: insurance came in near the high end, but cash pay collapsed and the guide was cut; stock -28.32%. The insurance line has never carried a print on its own; cash pay and the guide did.
findings.why_not_priced: The Street models the guided $25-31m. If the market expected an insurance beat, the stock would not have sat near the bottom of its post-print range ($5.42-7.66) until 2026-10-20 with put skew bid. It is also a segment line: insurance is about 15% of BetterHelp and 5% of the company, so even a clear beat moves consolidated revenue by under 1%. The cash-pay line is the swing, and net of it this is small.
findings.independence: BHB 2026-05-01 (https://bhbusiness.com/?p=11287) gives the Q1 run-rate of $75m+ on 14,000 sessions a week and 6,000 providers, the same company source one quarter earlier. The Q4 implied by the FY $90-105m insurance guide (about $34.5m, a run-rate near $140m) is also company arithmetic from the same release. No independent series.

findings.finding: The Street bar sits inside, and slightly below, the company's own Q3 guide: revenue $585.6m against a $569-609m guide (midpoint $589m), EPS -$0.23 against $(0.30)-$(0.20). The Q2 release says results were 'within our guidance ranges on a consolidated basis'. After a 5% FY revenue cut in July, this is a reset quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 (in-line quarter, guide held): +1.85%. Q2 2026 (in-line consolidated, guide cut): -28.32%. On this name the guide decides the sign, not the quarter's beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the bar is the guide, and the market was told to expect it. If a beat were expected, the bar would sit above the midpoint, and it does not. The residual is the usual cushion in a just-reset guide.
findings.independence: Company guide in https://s21.q4cdn.com/672268105/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/TDOC-2Q-2026-Earnings-Press-Release.pdf (one document for both the guide and the 'within guidance' claim).

findings.finding: Semrush shows betterhelp.com at 5.75m visits in July, 5.54m in August and 5.66m in September 2026: roughly flat through Q3, but well below the 7.25-8.31m monthly visits Semrush showed for Oct-Dec 2025. In September, paid search traffic fell 53% m/m and organic 17.5% m/m. This fits the guided mid-to-high-20% cut in ad spend. Top-of-funnel did not collapse further in Q3, but the September paid-search drop points to fewer new cash-pay sign-ups going into Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: BetterHelp cash-pay deterioration drove -28.32% (Q2 2026) and -13.56% (Feb 2025); stabilisation commentary drove +15.05% (Feb 2026).
findings.why_not_priced: Third-party traffic estimates are not in the wire copy, but the decline they show is what the company guided to (ad spend down mid-to-high 20%). It is a proxy for a line the company has already guided, so it is small. Semrush showed no Q2 2026 months, so the sequential comparison is unavailable.
findings.independence: Proxy only. Earlier Semrush snapshot (Oct-Dec 2025 visits) from search snippet of https://de.semrush.com/website/betterhelp.com/overview/ (dated 2026-01-13); the company's ad-spend guide on the Q2 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15364540438504448).

findings.finding: Short interest has risen five settlements in a row, from 23.69m shares (2026-08-14) to 32.07m (2026-10-15): 17.7% of shares outstanding and 8.2 days to cover. Since 2026-10-20 the stock has run about 16% ($5.73 to $6.655) on below-average volume with no catalyst named in any source. An in-line quarter with a held FY guide forces covering into thin liquidity, a squeeze mechanism of its own.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Feb 2026: guide held and a stabilisation story, +15.05%. Oct 2025: +6.2%. In 2024 Jefferies cited about 16% short as a short-term opportunity. When the guide was cut (Q2 2026), the short paid: -28%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the 16% run-up into the print may already be covering, and the put skew says the options market still leans down. If the squeeze were fully priced, short interest would have fallen at the 10-30 settlement (not yet published) and the skew would have flattened. It has not.
findings.independence: MarketBeat 2026-10-20 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-teladoc-health-nyse-tdoc-stock-jumps-81-time-to-buy-2026-10-20/): +8.1% on volume 63% below average with no catalyst. Earnings Whispers 2026-10-20 gave the $5.73 price.

findings.finding: $1.0bn of 1.25% convertible notes due 2027-06-01 is now classified as current; holders may convert freely from 2026-12-01. Against it: cash $774.3m at 2026-06-30, an undrawn $300m revolver ($297.2m available), FY FCF guide $130-170m, net leverage 0.8x. Management excluded 'any potential impact from changes in our current debt structure' from guidance and has not announced a refinancing. Lesson 4's question, what the money buys: it refinances an existing maturity and funds no ramp. Cash plus FCF plus the revolver covers it without equity, so this is not distress. A new instrument at today's rates would raise interest cost well above 1.25%. Net: near zero, slightly negative.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on financing since the 2025 repayment of $550.6m of notes, which was cash-funded with no dilution.
findings.why_not_priced: The maturity is public. What is not known is whether the Q3 call announces a plan and its form. A dilutive convert would show up as a fall on the day; a cash paydown plus revolver would remove the overhang. Neither has been signalled by any 8-K (no Item 1.01/2.03 filed since July).
findings.independence: Panabee Q2 2026 write-up (https://www.panabee.com/news/teladoc-health-earnings-q2-2026-report) on the same $1bn current classification. It rests on the same 10-Q.

findings.finding: All of Teladoc's remaining goodwill, $283.2m, sits in the BetterHelp reporting unit. The Q2 guide cut was treated as a triggering event, and the quantitative test found fair value above carrying value, with no headroom disclosed. The Q2 release added 'potential impairment of BetterHelp goodwill' as a named risk factor. Market cap is about $1.2bn (181.7m shares at $6.655) and has stayed below book. A further cash-pay miss in Q3 makes an interim impairment possible. It would be a non-cash, below-adj.-EBITDA item but a GAAP EPS miss against the -$0.23 bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2025 included a $59.1m Integrated Care impairment, stock -2.78% on that print; Q3 2025 a $12.6m impairment, stock +6.2%. Recent impairments here have not set the sign.
findings.why_not_priced: The risk is disclosed, but no one has quantified the headroom. If the market expected an impairment, GAAP EPS estimates would sit below the -$0.30 guide low, and they sit at -$0.23. A one-off with no path to the guide, so it is sized at a fraction.
findings.independence: Q2 release risk-factor list (https://s21.q4cdn.com/672268105/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/TDOC-2Q-2026-Earnings-Press-Release.pdf), the same company's documents.

findings.finding: Management and board turnover since the last print. Michael Grasher (insurance-industry CFO, ex-IFG/Fortegra/AMERISAFE) was named CFO effective immediately on 2026-08-31, after a long interim period, so this is his first earnings call. The Chief Legal Officer resigned 'with good reason' under his severance agreement (8-K 2026-09-24, effective 2026-11-01). One director retired on 2026-09-30 and a new director with Verisk insurance/analytics background was appointed 2026-08-03. A new CFO's first outlook, including any 2027 framing (Teladoc One goes broadly available January 2027), tends to set a conservative base.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on this name for a CFO's first call. The Q2 2026 guide cut (-28%) shows what a guide reset costs here.
findings.why_not_priced: The appointments are public 8-Ks, but the 'good reason' wording on the CLO exit is not in any preview I found. Whether a new CFO kitchen-sinks is an inference with no document behind it, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: CLO 8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1477449/000147744926000046/tdoc-20260924.htm (2026-09-24); director 8-Ks https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1477449/000147744926000042/tdoc-20260810.htm and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1477449/000147744926000040/exhibit9916.htm. baseline_tension: My small net positive (low bar, conservative insurance guide, crowded rising short) cuts against the +11.3 put skew, and the 16% run-up into the print has likely spent part of the squeeze. The option market's case is the July -28% reaction to an unobservable cash-pay line, and I found nothing that refutes it, so p_up sits at 52 rather than in the 55-60 band.
lessons_applied: Lesson 9 (segment net of the rest): insurance-beat finding cut +1.0 -> +0.6, because insurance is about 5% of revenue and cash pay is the swing.
Lesson 6 (inside the guide): bar-below-midpoint finding cut +1.0 -> +0.4; the bar is the company guide and the market was told to expect it.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): convert finding cut -0.5 -> -0.2 after answering it. The money refinances an existing maturity, is covered by cash, FCF and the revolver, and there is no distress.
Lesson 2 (one-offs): goodwill impairment risk kept as a one_off and cut -0.5 -> -0.4; non-cash, no path to the guide.
Lesson 5 (inference): new-CFO-conservatism finding cut -0.5 -> -0.3; no document behind the conservatism claim.
Lesson 7 (positioning): short-interest finding kept at +1.0 because the short is crowded (17.7%, rising). Against the 11.3-point put skew, p_up held at 52 rather than raised.
Breadth (searcher addendum): filed the Integrated Care deferral/implied-Q4 item and the routine ownership filings at 0.0 rather than leaving them out; abs_move and p_up unchanged.
